memory_verse.label: Memory Verse
memory_verse.text: "There is a lad here who has five barley loaves and two small fishes, but what are they among so many?" — John 6:9

devotion.label: Insight / Reflection
devotion.text:
We often hesitate to act because we feel what we have is insufficient. We look at our limited time, our small talent, or our meager resources and think they couldn’t possibly make a difference. However, the miracle of the five loaves and two fish teaches us a vital lesson: God doesn't require us to have everything; He only asks for our "something." When the young boy offered his small lunch, it seemed insignificant against the needs of thousands, yet in the hands of the Creator, that small gift was multiplied into an abundance that fed a multitude with baskets to spare.
This same principle is seen in the story of the widow at Zarephath. In the midst of a devastating famine, she had only a handful of flour and a little oil barely enough for one last meal for herself and her son. Yet, she chose to give out of her "something" first. Because she didn't let the smallness of her resource stop her from being obedient, God multiplied her supply so that it did not run dry until the rain returned. Her small act of faith became the very thing that sustained her life through the darkest days.
God is looking for what you have in your hand right now. Do not talk yourself out of a miracle by thinking your contribution is too small or your effort is too minor. Whether it is a moment of prayer, a small seed of finance, or a simple act of service, give it to Him with a willing heart. God needs your "something" to make "many things" out of it. When you release what you have, you give Heaven the material to create an overflow that you could never produce on your own.

quote.label: Today's Quote
quote.text: "If you cannot do great things, do small things in a great way." — Napoleon Hill

prayer.label: Prayer
prayer.text: Lord, I thank You that You are the God of the multiplication. Forgive me for the times I held back because I thought my gift was too small. Today, I place my "five loaves and two fish" into Your hands. Use my small beginnings, my little strength, and my modest resources to bring glory to Your name and to bless others. I trust You to multiply it in abundance. Amen.

conclusion.label: A Word to You
text: Never measure the potential of your gift by its size; measure it by the Greatness of the One you are giving it to. Your "little" becomes "much" the moment you let it go.
